verdict.rationale: LiveKit's core server is open source and ships as a self-deployable single binary, Docker image, or Kubernetes deployment. First-party docs cover self-hosting topics such as ports and firewall setup, and say users can move between Cloud and self-hosted without rewriting code. A community user also describes it as the right choice for a modern SFU you run yourself. Missing for 10: in-depth self-hosting production guides in the evidence (scaling, TURN, and whether agents, egress, and telephony are all self-hostable), plus clarity on which Cloud-only features (Inference, Agent Builder, Phone Numbers) are unavailable when self-hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Easy to deploy: single binary, Docker or Kubernetes
You can move from LiveKit Cloud to self-hosted if your requirements change.
It's possible to handle all UDP traffic on a single port.
LiveKit is an open-source platform for building voice, video, and physical AI agents.
